name: Aurocet
description: Aurocet is Lazarus's military-grade adrenal optimization compound, combining a fourth-generation synthetic catecholamine cascade with a proprietary SNT-adjacent neural primer that synchronizes the adrenal response with BCI tactical overlays, ensuring that the physiological surge aligns precisely with the moment of engagement rather than building unpredictably. The result is a surgical adrenal event — full combat chemistry delivered on demand, coordinated with the user's augmentation suite. It is not available to civilians through any legal channel.
effects: Precisely timed and calibrated adrenal surge on BCI-triggered demand
Cardiac output increase of approximately 40% without arrhythmia risk
Seamless integration with tactical BCI overlays enhancing situational awareness
Full physical combat enhancement without the cognitive impairment of uncontrolled adrenaline
Sustained performance plateau rather than spike-and-crash cycle
Minimal cortisol interference preserving post-combat cognitive function
side_effects: Requires compatible BCI — non-integrated use produces uncontrolled adrenal flooding
Hypertensive crisis if user's augmentation suite is damaged during the effect window
Long-term endocrine disruption — the body's natural adrenal production atrophies with sustained use
Psychological dependency on the precision of the effect — users describe unmedicated states as 'blunt' and 'inadequate'
Classified side effects not disclosed in available documentation
street_price: Φ1,200+ per injector on black market
cultural_context: Aurocet is the gold standard — the thing every Shelf runner has heard of and almost none have touched. When an injector appears on the black market, it moves fast and the provenance is always suspicious. Military contractors who've used it describe a qualitative difference from civilian combat drugs: not just more effective, but more coherent, like the drug and the body are finally speaking the same language. Lazarus guards the synthesis pathway aggressively — several corporate espionage operations have targeted it, and at least two Shelf chemists who got close to reverse-engineering it have disappeared.
story_hooks: A runner is offered a job that comes with two Aurocet injectors as part of the payment — the client has military connections, the job involves a Lazarus facility, and the drug itself may be evidence of something the runner shouldn't know.

A street version of Aurocet is circulating — it has the right packaging and the right feel, but without BCI integration it produces uncontrolled adrenal flooding. Someone is selling military packaging around a dangerous civilian compound, and people are dying.

A recently discharged military operative is selling Aurocet injectors to fund their transition to civilian life — they have forty units and a Lazarus military contracts officer who is hunting them very quietly.
